newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two foreign brokerage companies were raided by police yesterday on suspicion they started the remour that five local commercial banks are on the verge of collapse. The accusation against ABN-Amro Hoare Govett and Capital Nomura Securities Plc was made by Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yubamrung in parliament yesterday hours after police raided the firms on Sathorn road. (BANGKOK POST)

- South African President Nelson Mandela yesterday said his country would follow the lead of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in its approach toward political conflicts in Burma and Cambodia. He said that an "eminent regional leader" had suggested to him that a peace broker be sent to Burma to "quietly" persuade the ruling junta there to commence dialogues with democracy activists led by Aung San Suu Kyi, herself a Nobel Prize Winner. (THE NATION)

- Bangkok Bank has restructured and increased its fixed-deposit rates by at least 75 basis points, effective immediately. Annual interest rates on three- and six-month fixed deposits will now range from 11 percent to 11.75 percent, with 12-month rates at 8.75 percent. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thai Airways International is preparing to launch a second public offering with the aim of attracting investors from the U.S., Japan and Europe for 200 to 250 million shares, including 100 million new shares intended for a capital increase. Besides the capital increase, the PO will include 100 to 150 million shares to be sold by the Finance Ministry, which currently holds 87 percent of the national flag carrier. (THE NATION)
